title: I/O APIC redirection table entry
summary: An I/O APIC redirection table entry (RTE) is 8 bytes (64 bits). It routes an external interrupt to a CPU. Fields: vector (8 bits), delivery mode (3 bits: fixed, lowest priority, SMI, NMI, INIT, ExtINT), destination mode (physical/logical), delivery status (idle/pending), polarity (active high/low), remote IRR (for level-triggered), trigger mode (edge/level), mask (disabled/enabled), destination (8 bits = APIC ID or logical ID).

ext.summary: An I/O APIC redirection table entry (RTE) is 8 bytes (64 bits). It routes an external interrupt to a CPU. Fields: vector (8 bits), delivery mode (3 bits: fixed, lowest priority, SMI, NMI, INIT, ExtINT), destination mode (physical/logical), delivery status (idle/pending), polarity (active high/low), remote IRR (for level-triggered), trigger mode (edge/level), mask (disabled/enabled), destination (8 bits = APIC ID or logical ID).

structure.meaning: Interrupt vector (0-255). Delivered to the CPU.
000 fixed, 001 lowest priority, 010 SMI, 011 reserved, 100 NMI, 101 INIT, 110 reserved, 111 ExtINT.
0 = physical (destination = APIC ID), 1 = logical (destination = logical ID).
For level-triggered: 1 = interrupt received, not yet EOI'd.
APIC ID (physical mode) or logical ID (logical mode).

notes: I/O APIC replaces the 8259 PIC for routing external interrupts.
Each IRQ has a redirection table entry (RTE).
Level-triggered interrupts require EOI to clear the remote IRR bit.
I/O APIC supports up to 24 IRQs (or more on some systems).
MSI/MSI-X bypasses I/O APIC (device writes directly to local APIC).
